title: Picta x Astralite baby (final, verifier fixes applied): Picta's own colour filters re-tuned on Picta's clocks toward Astralite's dawn, day and dusk tones with brightness locked, plus Astralite's fog air (half strength first), distant mist rings and Mists of Tamriel banks
pitch: The baby is Picta. Exposure, the grade, night lighting, interiors, seasons, the summer weathers, the fair, the Helios exits and every fog distance stay as they are. What changes is colour, inside Picta's brightness. In Picta's dawn and dusk windows (06:00-09:00 and 17:00-20:00), the cold blue-violet horizon, the distant fog and the cloud undersides turn pink. They go magenta-pink in clear weather and a softer rose in cloudy weather (A01 at 07:30: horizon hue 281 -> 333, fog 278 -> 335; C01: 282 -> 348). The sky toward the sun turns rose. Shade light turns violet-mauve in clear weather and only slightly more violet in cloudy weather. By day the sky stays blue, just a little softer. Some things keep Picta's colour. Dawn and dusk sunlight stays Picta's coral. The sunlit cloud tops near the sun stay salmon-coral. In rain, fog and snow the sky and the distant fog keep Picta's blue but go greyer, and the cloud undersides pick up a faint grey-rose at dusk, as Astralite's do. Summer weathers keep their full warm lead over the base weathers. On top come Astralite's air and mists: coloured volumetric fog air (peach, gold or grey) at half Astralite's strength to start, faint distant mist rings on 15 weathers, and Mists of Tamriel valley mist banks on 12 clear, cloudy and foggy weathers. The rings and banks belong to the weather, so they also show at night, lit only by Picta's night light. Why this way: in Bottled every on-screen colour is a record colour times an Effects 11 filter, and Picta keeps its hue in the filters. Dropping Astralite's records under those filters would double-tint and break brightness (near fog 21x brighter). So each channel keeps one hue carrier, the one Picta already uses, re-solved every 15 minutes through the real Bottled chain to keep Picta's luminance. On the written 4-decimal files, every sky, cloud, sun-glow, fog, sunlight and ambient value stays within 0.61% of Picta's brightness. An independent model on the written files, under two alternative engine timing rules, keeps it within 0.95%. Night colour values are byte-identical, and with every mix at 0 the files equal Picta's. Two limits are stated plainly. First, when the light changes hue, warm surfaces in shade (skin, brown rock) get up to about 5% brighter at dawn and dusk, and greens up to 2% darker. Second, the fog air is a real brightness addition whose full size can only be judged in game. "Too strong" is fixed by amplitude dials, which weaken a colour without changing which colour it is.

colour_levers.periods: Effects 11 Dawn, Sunrise, Day, Sunset, Dusk in the 24 routed exterior files (21 masters + 3 summer). Night and Interior periods are never written.
colour_levers.lever: [SKY] GradientTopColorFilter{Dawn..Dusk}, written with 4 decimals. Record SkyUpperColor stays Picta grey.
colour_levers.math: V(h) = desat(rec^GradientTopCurve * F(h) * GradientTopIntensity * GradientIntensity, GradientDesaturation(h)), with F(h) = sum_p w_p(h) F_p (Bottled TOD weights, Day^0.6 bend), solved jointly over 05:30-20:30 every 15 minutes. Target T(h) is a mix of V_Picta(h) and V_Astralite(h): Astralite's partner record on Picta's climate times its Soul Core grade, held at Picta's luminance. The mix is made in OKLab. Hue follows the short OKLCh arc when the two hues are within 120 deg, follows the straight a,b line through grey when they are 170 deg or more apart, and blends smoothly in between (smoothstep on |dh|). Near-opposite hues therefore mix through grey and never jump sides between steps. alpha(h) = sum_s CLMT_s(h)*MIX_s, normalised so the on-screen share at 07:30/13:00/18:30 equals the MIX label (A01 sky needed 0.638 in the dawn/dusk slots to reach 0.54). The final chroma is multiplied by STRENGTH_slot*KAPPA_SKY (hue fixed). Least squares: chromaticity rows (V-T)/Y_P with weight 1, luminance rows with weight 10. Clamp [0,10]. Values within 5e-5 of Picta keep Picta's text. All audits run on the 4-decimal values actually written. Fair weathers (19FA01, 19FA02, 19FB02, 19FC01) are solved on Picta's climate and on the fair climate (05:30-10:00 / 16:00-20:30) together. Summer weathers aim at Astralite's colour shifted by Picta's own summer-minus-master offset. A01: Dawn 0.098, 0.176, 0.373 -> 0.1152, 0.1676, 0.3916; Day 0.0314, 0.169, 0.404 -> 0.043, 0.1645, 0.4115. Worst band luminance change: 0.03%.
colour_levers.why: Picta's sky hue lives in this TIMEOFDAY key and the record under it is grey. Changing the same key on the same clock adds no new record x ini cross-term, and at MIX 0 it reproduces Picta exactly. Resolved: the near-opposite-hue flip found by the verifier (D01/D02/E02/E05/E06 clouds jumping about 95 deg between steps) is fixed by the hybrid mix. Over all 28 weathers, the largest 15-minute colour step is now 0.022 OKLab (A01 fog at 20:15, Picta's own largest is 0.010), and there are no flips.

colour_levers.channel: sky horizon band (dominates the dome through AirGlow 1000)
colour_levers.why: This band carries the twilight ring. The fit puts Astralite's coral-pink in the Dusk period (17:00-20:30, matching Picta's climate sunset window), so the Sunset period, which bleeds into the afternoon, stays near day tones.

colour_levers.lever: No lever. SkyLowerColor, GradientMiddle* and the global UseProceduralGradientWeights=true are untouched.
colour_levers.math: Dome = lerp(top, horizon, (1-z)^ProceduralGradientWeightCurve). The lower band never reaches the screen.
colour_levers.why: Turning the global flag off would reshape every Picta dome. The mid-sky mauve comes back on its own from the indigo-to-rose gradient.

colour_levers.lever: [SKY] CloudsColorFilter{Dawn..Dusk}. Cloud layer records stay Picta. Picta's tie CloudsColorFilter == FogColorFilter is released on purpose: each is solved to its own target.
colour_levers.math: Corrected order (Sky.hlsl 426): V = desat(rec^CloudsCurve, CloudsDesaturation) * CloudsIntensity * CloudsColorFilter. The old solver desaturated after the filter; there is no impact today because CloudsDesaturation Dawn..Dusk = 0 in all 24 files, but a later Picta change would have been mis-solved. Same hybrid mix and least squares as the sky, KAPPA_CLOUDS, plus an RGB-mean row (weight 3) that holds the brightness of the sun-rim term (ShadeCloud adds the rim in proportion to the cloud's RGB mean, not its luminance). A01: Dawn 0.353, 0.373, 0.765 -> 0.5983, 0.3285, 0.4945; Dusk 0.353, 0.349, 0.765 -> 0.6449, 0.2893, 0.5012; Day 0.157, 0.353, 0.863 -> 0.2248, 0.349, 0.7151. C01 Dawn 0.294, 0.373, 0.765 -> 0.6414, 0.3016, 0.4549. Cloud base luminance at most 0.32%.
colour_levers.why: Astralite's rose dawn cloud decks and whiter day clouds. Without the mean row, the silver-lining rim near the sun lost up to 13%. With it, the rim moves at most 7.4% (C04 at 18:45) and 5.9% (A01). A heavier mean row (10) holds the rim within 1.8%, but it locks cloud chroma onto a blue-or-rose line and stops rain and fog clouds from going grey, so it was rejected.

colour_levers.channel: sun-side glow and the light on sunlit clouds (sky scattering colour)
colour_levers.lever: [SKYSCATTERING] ScatteringColor{Dawn..Dusk} only. ColorFromSun is now UNTOUCHED, and so are SunColorFilter, MoonColorFilter, SunDesaturation, the record SunColor, Intensity, Amount, AirGlow* and Dust*.
colour_levers.math: S(view) = (1+(sunN-1)*CFS) * ScatteringColor * sunFade * Intensity * Pow32(1 - dustBand(view) * DustTint), with DustTint_ch = max(0, 1-c_ch/cmax)*2*DustDensity^2. The solve is a 6-iteration fixed point with luminance weight 100 on two views together: the sunward horizon (z = 0.05, the sky glow) and the sun direction itself (elevation = sunZ^2, no aboveHorizon or DustDarkening, times saturate(Amount^2)). The sun-direction view is GetScatteringColorAt(sunDir), which ShadeCloud adds to every sunlit cloud (SkyScattering.hlsli 218-228) and which the cloud silver lining uses. A01: Dawn 1, 1, 1 -> 0.9557, 1.0464, 0.6769; Day -> 1.0891, 0.9823, 0.9312; Dusk -> 0.9663, 1.0471, 0.6545. Sunward dome pixel at most 0.06%; sun glow at the horizon 0.59%; cloud light at the sun 0.35%; sunlit cloud total (base + light, texture 0.7) 0.32%. The independent model on the written files gives 0.95% under the alternative sun path.
colour_levers.why: Resolved, verifier major 1: the sunlit-cloud term was outside the old audit and moved 1.0-2.9%. Testing showed the ColorFromSun lerp is what made the two views impossible to hold together (still 1.7-2.4% with weight 400). With ColorFromSun at Picta's value, both hold within 0.6%, and the sky toward the sun still reaches rose-pink (A01 07:30 hue 301 -> 350, on-screen share 0.50). The cost: sunlit cloud tops near the sun keep Picta's saturated salmon-coral (29 -> 41 hue at 07:30) instead of Astralite's paler tone. KAPPA_SCAT can soften them.

colour_levers.lever: [ENVIRONMENT] FogColorFilter{Dawn..Dusk}. FogColorFilterAmount stays 0. FogColorMultiplier, FogColorCurve, FogAmountMultiplier, FogCurveMultiplier and the FogNear/FogFar records are untouched.
colour_levers.why: Rose-pink aerial perspective at twilight. One filter serves near and far fog; Picta's near fog record is almost black, so the far fog carries the hue.

colour_levers.lever: [ENVIRONMENT] DirectLightingColorFilter{Dawn..Dusk} only. DirectLightingDesaturation, Intensity, Curve and the SunlightColor records are untouched.
colour_levers.math: V(h) = diag(desat(rec_sunlight(h on the Picta and, for fair weathers, the fair climate), DLDesat(h)) * DLInt(h)) @ F(h). Luminance is locked every 15 minutes against the actual hourly record sunlight. The luminance weight steps 100 -> 400 -> 1000 -> 3000 until the worst step is at most 0.5% (A01 used 400). Brightness normalisation applies to the Day slot only. A01: Day 0.98, 0.941, 0.902 -> 0.9889, 0.9373, 0.9128; Dawn 0.98, 0.392, 0 -> 0.9755, 0.3957, 0; Dusk 0.98, 0.314, 0 -> 0.9768, 0.3176, 0. Worst sunlight luminance: 0.45% (E01 at 18:30).
colour_levers.why: Kept from the previous final (no DirectLightingDesaturation lift: it cost 4-5% brightness and bought no dawn hue once luminance is locked). Dawn and dusk sunlight stays Picta's coral, because Picta's sunrise sunlight colour has no blue. Midday light moves part way to Astralite's softer pinkish-white.

colour_levers.periods: record slots Sunrise, Day, Sunset (Night slot untouched), on Picta's climate 06-09/17-20, plus the fair climate for the 4 fair weathers
colour_levers.lever: Baby ESL: WTHR DirectionalAmbientLightingColors.{Sunrise,Day,Sunset}.Directional{X,Y,Z}{Plus,Minus} on the 28 weathers (468 field ops). Specular, Scale, Fresnel, AmbientLightingIntensity and AmbientLightingDesaturation are untouched (E11 4ca678b has no ambient colour filter).
colour_levers.math: Per axis, the 3 slots x RGB are solved jointly over every 15-minute step: V(h) = AmbInt(h) * Dm(AmbDesat(h)) @ (sum_s CLMT_s(h) r_s + CLMT_N r_N). Rows: chromaticity toward the mixed target (weight 1), light luminance (weight 20), and NEW albedo-weighted luminance rows for foliage, pine, brown dirt, grey stone, snow and skin (weight 4, the AMB_SURFACE_LOCK dial). Then a gamut guard at 254.4 and a +-1 integer search per channel that scores light luminance plus a quarter of the worst surface error. A01 Sunrise X+ 63,67,137 -> 87,63,108, Z- 76,95,195 -> 111,89,156, Day X+ 28,63,154 -> 33,63,146. C01 Sunrise X+ 50,63,129 -> 61,63,103. D03 Sunrise X+ 70,88,148 -> 80,88,122. Worst light luminance: 0.61% (C01 Z- at 18:45) on Picta's clock, 0.71% on the fair clock.
colour_levers.why: Records are the only ambient colour carrier, on the clock Astralite authored DALC for. E11-managed IBL is on in exteriors, so the sky also reaches ambient through the sky-IBL term (proxy at most 0.03%). Resolved, verifier major 5: holding the light's luminance does not hold the brightness of coloured surfaces. With the albedo rows, the surface change in shade at dawn and dusk is at most skin +4.7%, brown rock +3.9%, foliage +2.3%, pine -1.6%, and grey stone and snow within 0.7%. Before the rows it was skin +6.3%. Locking every albedo would erase the hue change (three independent albedos fix RGB completely). Weight 10 cuts skin to +2.6% but leaves shade blue-violet (A01 dawn hue 294 instead of 310).

colour_levers.lever: [GAMEVOLUMETRICRAYS] ColorFilter{Dawn..Dusk} = luminance-equal grey Y(F_Picta)*(1,1,1). A01: Dawn 0.98, 0.392, 0 -> 0.489 grey; Day -> 0.946 grey; Dusk -> 0.433 grey. Desaturation and RangeFactor untouched.
colour_levers.math: VL colour = desat(lerp(graded sunlight, VOLI colour, CustomColorContribution), GVR Desat) * GVR ColorFilter (ISCompositeLensFlareVolumetricLighting.hlsl 35-41).
colour_levers.why: Removes the double tint on Astralite's VOLI colour, and keeps Picta's own crossfade VL luminance (a 1,1,1 filter would have doubled it at dawn).

colour_levers.lever: Untouched: ColorFromSun, DirectLightingDesaturation, GVR RangeFactor, SunColorFilter, MoonColorFilter, the sun disc, IMGS tints (no copies), [VOLUMETRICFOG] ColorFilter, EffectLightingColor, WaterMultiplierColor, SkyStaticsColor (optional switch below, off), every Intensity, Curve, AirGlow, Amount, FogAmount, FogColorMultiplier, AmbientLighting, ColorCorrection, KiSuite and adaptation key, ProceduralGradientWeightCurve, CLMT, REGN, all Night keys and slots, all Interior periods, the 13 MQ files, the base enbseries.ini (alive branch), the interior templates and _locationweather.ini.
colour_levers.math: Byte-identical. Measured difference of every E11 night value, DALC night slot and VOLI night slot from 20:30 to 05:30 over all 28 weathers: 0.0 (both models).
colour_levers.why: Night was not offered; interiors and brightness are locked. The night PICTURE is not identical, because the mist rings and MoT banks are weather-level fields with no hour gate (see fog_mist and user choice 4). Rejected again: grey IMGS copies (they change Picta's grade) and a re-hue of [VOLUMETRICFOG] (Bottled applies it only to non-effect-lit meshes, and every fog and mist mesh here is effect-lit).

colour_levers.channel: sky statics colour (Picta mountain fog + MoT banks), optional
colour_levers.lever: Baby ESL SkyStaticsColor, OFF by default (values precomputed in records_manifest.json optional_off_by_default)
colour_levers.math: Y-locked hybrid mix toward Astralite SkyStaticsColor at MIX.
colour_levers.why: Kept as an option until an in-game check confirms the engine applies this colour to the statics. The mist meshes already pick up the new tones through scene light.

pairing:

It is read off-order with houseCARL, source pinned to {file:'Astralite ENB.esp', mod:'[NoDelete] Soul Core Plugin and Assets'}, and is never enabled or mastered. VOLIs that Astralite ENB.esp does not override are read from Astralite Weathers.esp. Soul Core E11 values are used only as model inputs (Astralite's visible chroma and its VL-to-key-light ratio). They are never copied as Picta scalars.

Ambient (DALC) follows the file's colour partner. Shared files are solved jointly over every weather they serve. NEW single rule (verifier 3 major): every mist component follows the mist partner's own fields. That means its VOLI per slot, its distant ring only where Picta's VisualEffect slot is free, and the 12 MoT bank statics only if the partner lists them. Result:
- SkyrimClear: banks only, no ring (A01, A03, B01, 5AFA01, 5AFA03, 5AFB01)
- SkyrimClear_A: Lite ring only, no banks (A02, B02, 5AFA02, 5AFB02)

fog_mist.component: Volumetric fog air (VOLI density + tint) and god rays
fog_mist.action: Create 11 new VOLI records in the baby ESL (PXA_LAM_*), one per Astralite source VOLI and Picta range group. Each copies every field of its PBR-winning source (colour, CustomColorContribution, DensityContribution, DensitySize, DensityWind/FallingSpeed, PhaseFunctionContribution/Scattering) except Intensity, and SamplingRepartitionRangeFactor, which is pinned to the Picta VOLI it replaces (100 or 80). Mixed groups are therefore split into _R100 and _R80 copies. Intensities, shared by every VL variant: PeachVL 2.337, DayVL 1.253, PureVL 2.074, YellowVL 1.388, GoldVL 1.179, FogVL_R100 1.437, FogVL_R80 1.625, FogVL_Blue_R100 1.614, FogVL_Blue_R80 1.899, StormVL_R100 1.272, StormVL_R80 1.266. Point VolumetricLighting.Sunrise/Day/Sunset of the 28 weathers at the mist partner's copies; Night keeps Picta's VOLI. In the 24 routed E11 files, solve GAMEVOLUMETRICRAYS Intensity{Dawn..Dusk} per file and set ColorFilter{Dawn..Dusk} to luminance-equal grey. RangeFactor is no longer written.
fog_mist.scaling: The regimes are translated, never mixed. Target = Astralite's own VL-to-key-light ratio at its slot peaks, retimed on Picta's climate and blended toward Picta's own ratio by the climate Night weight, times VOL_AMOUNT. The floor is Picta's god-ray ratio (alive branch). The solve includes the moon/sun crossfades and caps the baby at 1.10x target at every 15-minute step (worst 1.099). The VOLI copy intensities (K) are solved once at half strength and fixed, so half/full and alive/newly_on differ only in the E11 GVR lines. Half strength (default), alive, GVR Dawn..Dusk: A01 0.75/2/4/2/0.75 -> 1.259/3.037/9.158/3.016/1.284; C01 -> 2.272/9.356/11.103/10.319/1.842; D02 -> 1.816/18.116/37.536/17.565/2.56; D03 -> 1.21/21.124/65.587/19.7/1.779; E05 -> 2.089/24.472/51.555/24.65/2.085. Full strength (prebuilt): D03 Day 119.1, E05 98.6 (registered range 0-1000). Reached vs the half-strength target at 07:30/13:00/18:30: clear 0.66/1.00/0.68, cloudy 0.93/1.00/0.77, heavy fog 0.76/0.99/0.89, rain 0.91/0.99/1.01, heavy snow 0.72/0.98/0.75. Resolved, verifier majors V1-2 and V3-2: with range now equal to Picta's, the remaining unmodelled parts are DensityContribution (Picta 0, copies 0.85-1.0), the scattering phase, and ENB eye adaptation. So the 'x Picta' figures are intensity-only and are not guarantees. Half strength, intensity-only, dawn/noon: clear 3.2x/1.0x, cloudy 3.7x/1.5x, heavy fog 4.8x/1.3x, rain 4.3x/2.2x, heavy snow 7.5x/2.2x. Full strength: clear 3.9x/1.0x, cloudy 5.2x/2.9x, fog 7.9x/2.6x, rain 7.8x/4.0x, heavy snow 11.4x/4.3x.
fog_mist.visible_when: Exteriors, while the weather is current. Bottled VL ExteriorEnabled=true forces engine VL on in exteriors, and Effects11Priority=0 means E11 owns intensity (Effects11.cpp 729-735). Whether the Darkened plugin ini line fVolumetricLightingIntensity=0.0 mutes VL today cannot be proven offline, so both branches are prebuilt and verified at both strengths, and the in-game probe picks one. ALIVE (default): the plugin ini is a byte copy; only the routed Dawn..Dusk GVR Intensity and ColorFilter lines change. NEWLY_ON: the fork's plugin ini gets fVolumetricLightingIntensity=1.0, and GVR Intensity is 0 for every exterior period of the base ini, the 13 MQ files and B01_PictaPure, plus IntensityNight 0 in the 24 routed files. NEWLY_ON GVR A01 1.544/2.065/2.303/2.14/1.552, reaching 0.70/0.99/0.73 in clear weather. The ESL is the same in all four variants.
fog_mist.risk: This is the one deliberate brightness addition (the user's fog pick), and it starts at half strength. It also brings back, and goes past, the misty air on A03 (Clear Mist) and B03 (Misty Fog) that the Darkened 1.0.1 revert removed; a per-weather VOL 0 is available for them. Weather transitions (verifier minor, now audited): halfway through a change between a clear/storm weather and heavy fog or rain at midday, the haze can swell above the brighter end (E01 to D02 +105%, E03 to D03 +90%, C01 to C04 +57%, A01 to D03 +46%; at dawn and dusk at most +22%). Picta has no swell, and Astralite's own lane at most +7%. The verifier's fix (one GVR curve with per-weather VOLI copies, 80 copies) was tested and does not help (+113-123%), because the cause is VOLI intensity x sunlight, both lerped by the engine, not GVR. Keeping Picta's GVR with per-file copies removes the swell (+17%) but starves fog and rain haze to 9-29% of target, so it was rejected too. In newly_on, Picta's own night VOLI gets faint VL at 05:30-06:00 and 20:00-20:30 from the Dawn/Dusk GVR (up to 0.86 of the key light at half strength, 1.71 at full, E02 at 20:00), where Picta has none; this is now in the audit and stated. Sky Sync's under-horizon VL dimming is not modelled, and the engine's VOLI interpolation across climate slots is assumed linear.

fog_mist.component: Distant mist rings (camera-attached Distant_Mounts, via the WTHR VisualEffect slot)

Set VisualEffect with Begin/End (Lite 0/0, Heavy 0.498/0.498, Rain 0/0) by the single mist rule: Lite on A02, B02, 5AFA02, 5AFB02, C01; Heavy on B03, C03, D01, D02; Rain on C04, D03, D04, C05, D05, D06. That is 15 weathers. A01/A03/B01 and their summer twins no longer get a ring (their partner, SkyrimClear, has banks instead). C02 and E01-E06 keep Picta's needles. Distant_Rain 00081D and the storm-snow ring are not copied. Assets are byte copies (md5-verified) from '[NoDelete] Soul Core Plugin and Assets': meshes/effects/distant_mounts_lite.nif, distant_mounts_heavy.nif, distant_mounts_rain.nif and Textures/effects/Distant_Fogs_Lite.dds, Distant_Fogs_Heavy.dds, Distant_Fogs_Rain.dds.
fog_mist.scaling: None. The meshes are effect-lit, so their colour is texture x scene light, which already carries the baby's tones. Picta's [PARTICLE] LightingInfluence 0.15 / AmbientInfluence 0.35-0.5 are kept. The MIST_RINGS table is the amplitude lever.
fog_mist.visible_when: Always while a listed weather is current, at every hour including night (no time gate exists on this field), lit by scene light. There is no MCM or ini gate, and no Picta-lane mod ships these paths.
fog_mist.risk: The rings may read dimmer or flatter than in the PBR lane; raising [PARTICLE] keys would brighten all particles, so drop the ring per weather instead. The three distant_mounts NIFs are Skyrim LE format (stream 83) particle meshes that already run in the PBR lane. If a crash appears near a ring weather, they are the first suspect. risks.risk: The engine's record-colour interpolation on the climate (peak at the window midpoint) is assumed, not read from source. It sets alpha(h), the DALC hourly lock and the VL crossfade shape.
risks.mitigation: It is one function (clmt_weights). The independent model run under a plateau rule keeps every colour component within 0.95%. An in-game time-lapse at 06:30, 07:30 and 08:30 settles it; re-solve if it is off.

risks.risk: The model is pre-tonemap: SH2, KiSuite and adaptation are encrypted or unmodelled, so absolute screen values can differ.
risks.mitigation: Colour brightness is locked relative to Picta through the same downstream chain, so the difference cancels to first order for equal inputs. The same-save A/B is the acceptance test. Every taste dial is amplitude-only.

risks.risk: The fog air is a real, partly unmodelled brightness addition. The model counts intensity only (range is now pinned to Picta's), while density (Picta 0, copies 0.85-1.0), the scattering phase and ENB eye adaptation (EnableAdaptation=true) are outside it. Bright haze can lower exposure for everything else. Intensity-only, half strength: clear 3.2x Picta's god rays at dawn and about equal at noon, up to 7.5x/2.2x in heavy snow.
risks.mitigation: It starts at half strength, with full prebuilt as an E11-only switch, plus a DENSITY dial, per-weather off and 'off'. The A/B has an exposure check and a clear-noon away-from-sun haze shot. The user is told plainly.

risks.risk: Weather-transition haze swell: halfway through a change between a clear/storm weather and heavy fog or rain at midday, the haze can rise above the brighter end (E01 to D02 +105%, E03 to D03 +90%, C01 to C04 +57%, A01 to D03 +46%). Picta has none; Astralite's own lane at most +7%. The cause is the engine lerping VOLI intensity and sunlight together, while Picta's dim bad-weather sunlight needs strong haze records.
risks.mitigation: Two fixes were tested in scratch and rejected. One GVR curve with 80 per-weather copies leaves +113-123%. Picta's GVR with per-file copies gives +17% but leaves fog/rain haze at 9-29% of target. What remains: half strength halves the absolute size, per-weather VOL 0 for fog/rain, and an A/B item to watch one such change.

risks.risk: Whether VL renders today cannot be proven offline: the Darkened plugin ini has fVolumetricLightingIntensity=0.0, while bVolumetricLightingUpdateWeather=1 and Bottled forces exterior VL on. The newly_on fallback also assumes that ini value multiplies rather than replaces the per-weather VOLI.
risks.mitigation: All four variants are prebuilt and verified, and the ESL is identical in all of them. The 2-minute editor probe picks the branch, and a second check (peach at 07:30) tests the newly_on assumption.

user_choices.question: How strongly should Astralite's dawn, day and dusk colours be mixed into Picta? Brightness stays the same at every level; only the colour changes.
user_choices.options: Light: dawn and dusk horizons and distant fog turn a soft magenta-pink, shade turns slightly mauve, and the day sky is almost unchanged. Medium: clear dawns and dusks turn magenta-pink, cloudy ones a soft rose, shade in clear weather turns violet-mauve, and the day sky is a slightly softer blue. Strong: rose-pink horizons, salmon in cloudy weather, close to Astralite itself; brightness still holds within about 1%.
user_choices.recommended: Medium. If it ever looks too strong, the fix makes the colours weaker without changing which colours they are.

user_choices.question: Astralite's coloured fog air (peach at dawn, gold, grey in rain and fog) adds light to the scene. It is the one part of the baby that is brighter than Picta, and its full effect can only be judged in game. How strong should it start?
user_choices.options: Half of Astralite's strength / Astralite's full strength / off (then the mist comes only from the distant mist rings and the valley mist banks). Either strength can be switched later without touching the colours. Good to know: on the 'clear with mist' and 'misty fog' weathers this brings back the misty air that the Darkened brightness work removed, and those two can be left without it.
user_choices.recommended: Half strength first, then the in-game check (brightness, haze and one weather change into fog). Going to full later is a quick swap. If the game's volumetric lighting turns out to be off in Picta today, the baby turns it on only for these weathers.

user_choices.question: Rain, fog and snow weathers: should they also take Astralite's greyer colours, or keep Picta's colours with only the mists and fog air added?
user_choices.options: Mix them like the other weathers (their skies and distant fog keep Picta's blue but go greyer, and cloud undersides get a faint grey-rose at dusk) / keep Picta's colours in rain, fog and snow
user_choices.recommended: Mix them like the other weathers. That is what Astralite looks like there.

user_choices.question: Astralite's distant mist rings and the valley mist banks belong to the weather itself, so they show at every hour, including at night (faint, under Picta's night light). Keep them?
user_choices.options: Keep them at all hours, as Astralite does / drop the rings and banks and keep only the coloured fog air
user_choices.recommended: Keep them. They are part of the mists you picked, and at night they are only lit by Picta's own dim light.
